verdict.line: You lose extended trades before level 6 while Gnar pokes freely at range 1100; you win once Titanic Hydra is online and he has to respect your taunt.

brief.thesis: Gnar's mini-form Q (Boomerang Throw, range 1100) outranges Shen's Q (Vorpal Blade, range 475) by over double, and his E (Hop, 475 range) resets the trade by bouncing away before Shen's Shadow Dash (575 range, 16s cooldown at rank 1) can land. The 48.8% head-to-head over 1431 games and Gnar's lane/solo-kill edge both come from that early range and mobility mismatch, not from Shen being outclassed once items come online.

theirWindow.what: He can poke with Boomerang Throw at 1100 range and immediately Hop away if you close, so don't walk up for cheap trades — you'll eat a slow and damage with no way to punish.

yourWindow.what: Shadow Dash in to taunt. He can't disengage without E, so this is your one reliable window to land Q (Vorpal Blade) repeatedly and life-tap back the damage he dealt poking you.

start.why: 49.5% win rate over 1391 games and the 83% pick rate for this matchup — the flat damage reduction on hit directly answers Gnar's poke-heavy mini-form autos and his Boomerang Throw chip damage.

boots.why: 50.6% win rate over 1345 games, 84.3% pick rate. Gnar's value in both forms comes from auto-attack damage (Hyper procs and Mega Gnar autos), so the flat reduction outperforms Mercury's Treads here.

core.why: Gives you the wave-clear and sustained trading damage you're missing before this point — core to the 59.3% win-rate build path.
Second item in the measured 59.3% win-rate path; adds the durability needed to survive Mega Gnar's area stun once he transforms.
Third item in the top build path (59.3% over 81 games); punishes Gnar's attack-speed-reliant Hyper procs once he's forced to auto you.

your team wants more out of your Vorpal Blade life-tap heal in extended skirmishes
the game runs long and you need more raw health scaling over Thornmail's damage reflect

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the sustained trading pattern you're forced into against ranged poke — every proc heals you back some of what Gnar's Boomerang Throw took off, and it's the keystone behind the 51.6% win-rate page.

summoners.why: 51.4% win rate at 58.6% pick rate, the highest-performing combo in this matchup. Ignite punishes the moments mini Gnar overextends his poke range before he can Hop out of kill range.

playing.title: Respect the 1100-range poke
playing.detail: Don't approach for trades before you have E (Shadow Dash) at level 3 — Boomerang Throw hits you from well outside your own Q range and slows you for free.

playing.title: Dash when Hop is down
playing.detail: Shadow Dash the moment you see his E (Hop, 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s cooldown) go on cooldown. That's your only guaranteed taunt window before he can reposition out of range.

playing.title: Hold Feint for the hyped auto
playing.detail: Gnar's W (Hyper) procs bonus damage on attacks and spells every few hits. Time W (Feint) to absorb that specific burst rather than burning it on a normal poke.

playing.title: Track Rage before you commit
playing.detail: Watch his Rage bar climb toward max — once he transforms, Mega Gnar's W stuns in an area around him, so don't walk into melee range right as he's about to flip.

playing.title: Use Q to offset the early range deficit
playing.detail: Vorpal Blade's cooldown drops to 4s at max rank and life-taps every hit — spam it whenever you're in range to claw back health he took from range before you could close.

playing.title: Don't force the lane after level 6
playing.detail: Stand United's 25000 range lets you abandon a losing lane for a teleport play elsewhere on the map — if the lane stays even, your ultimate's global impact is worth more than another risky all-in.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, build paths, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.19.1) via OP.GG; the cooldowns, ranges, and tactical reasoning connecting them are my own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Gnar’s (Q). Absorb the third (W) basic attack with [W]. Engage aggressively whenever Gnar’s (E) is on cooldown. Be careful of Gnar’s chained CC skills when he transforms into Mega Gnar.
